text:
hiro: Heads up — bringing up a new model conversion path. Converted Nimbus-13B (orig Qwen format) to our Llama-compatible runtime and ran int4 quant + evals. Seeing a consistent ROUGE/ROUGE-L drop on long-doc summarization (~6-8 pts) vs float32 baseline.

matt: ugh. reproduction steps? small diff or huge? :eyes:

hiro: repro steps clipped below. quick summary: conversion uses our usual qwen->llama mapping script, then run quantize.py --mode int4 --calib=256k. Serving via dedicated dev pool. Shortbench shows token latency fine but quality regressed on docs >2k tokens.

hiro: ```bash
# conversion (simplified)
python convert_qwen_to_llama.py --input nimbus13b.bin --out nimbus13b.llama --map-heads auto
python quantize.py --model nimbus13b.llama --dtype int4 --calib-samples 256000
redwood serve --model nimbus13b.int4 --profile long-summarize
```

ana: can you paste a harmful example or diff in outputs? might be vocab mismatch or rotaries.

hiro: here's a short sample pair (float32 vs int4) for a 3.2k token doc:

float32: "Executive summary: the committee recommends a phased rollout..."
int4: "Executive summary: the committee recommends immediate adoption..."

hiro: note: factual change and hallucinated timeline added. eval harness shows drop on factuality metrics too.

priya: did you try disabling any rotary scaling hacks? we had a headwise scale toggle landed in runtime last month.

hiro: good call — toggled runtime flag --rotary-head-scale=off and re-ran. regression disappears (scores match within noise). So it's tied to how headwise rotary scaling is applied for this converted model.

matt: interesting. so conversion + quantization exposed a sensitivity to headwise scaling. could be aliasing of freq table across head dims after packing.

priya: I can run a quick per-head sanity test. small snippet I use:

```py
# compute cosine between head rotary bases (float vs quant simulation)
def head_base_diff(base_f32, base_qsim):
    return np.linalg.norm(base_f32 - base_qsim, axis=-1).mean()

# iterate heads and print large diffs
```

priya: if differences are concentrated on some heads that explains why disabling head-scale helps.

ana: also double-check token id mapping — Nimbus used a custom tie that shifts BOS/EOS indices by 1 in the Qwen arch. conversion script claims to remap but tiny misalignments with prefix caching can create drift over long contexts.

hiro: confirmed token ids are aligned; ran unit test across 1M tokens and counts match. failing only when both head-scale enabled AND int4 packing. float32+head-scale OK, int4+no-head-scale OK.

matt: that screams packing order bug. int4 repack rearranges per-head data into word-aligned blocks; if headwise scale metadata isn't applied in that same packing order we get head mismatch.

hiro: logged an issue: https://console.redwood.ai/issue/RI-2026 — attached conversion artifacts + quant tables.

ci-bot: build 2026.2 triggered: tests/quant-pipeline::nimbus-int4-smoke started. (will post results)

priya: taking a quick look at the quant table blobs now. If anyone has time, try a targeted revert: in quantizer change packing_order from 'head-major' to 'block-major' and run the sanity harness.

ana: FYI I saw a similar pattern on a different model where rotary_freq scaling was applied per-head but serialization flattened heads in pairs — produced subtle phase swaps. There we fixed by adding header metadata to the bin and validating a small checksum in runtime.

hiro: thanks — I'll try the packing_order tweak and checksum in conversion. will post results.

matt: if you want I can spin a tiny dev job to run full long-doc eval overnight. cc @priya.

hiro: please do. attaching quick perf diff from local runs:

```
Model           ROUGE-L
nimbus13b-f32   42.8
nimbus13b-int4  36.1  <-- regressed
nimbus13b-int4 (no-head-scale) 42.5
```

priya: great signal. thanks. I'll open a patch for the quantizer to keep packing consistent with head metadata.

ana: thanks team. ping me if you want me to QA with our longctx dataset. :+1:

hiro: will do. marking thread for follow-up after CI finishes. :spiral_calendar:
